scope: Local, shared-development and drill producer proof, and the restricted backup host's commands. This file grants no external or production authority. docs/runbooks/recovery.md is the operator's runbook.

commands.app_key_probe: node ops/maintenance/cli.mts bucket-probe --config <private-directory> --keys production=<private-env-file> --keys preview=<private-env-file> --keys development=<private-env-file>

control.file: Regular, non-symlink, current OS user owned, no group or other permissions, outside checkout.
control.identity: Current uid and hostname, unexpired exact operation list and development context.
control.database: Pinned shared-development direct endpoint plus matching current database, role and explicit schema. Neither a URL nor a sentinel alone grants authority. The --config commands pin host, database, role and schema the same way and classify the host as disposable, drill, development or production; production is refused without the owner's approval in control.json.
control.migration_role: Operator only. The application runtime cannot create schema objects or update migration history.
control.directory: The --config commands read control.json, source.env, backup.key and the bucket key from one private directory: mode 700, current OS user owned, outside the checkout.

migration_provenance.deployment_path: Vercel project everyfield has root apps/web and default Next build. app build/start and managed previews do not run migrations. CI migrates its throwaway database explicitly.
migration_provenance.automatic_replay: Only a complete matching ordered checksum prefix is replayed. Unknown, missing or changed checksums refuse before application.
migration_provenance.adoption: Separately review the exact existing rows and SQL hashes. The explicit command preserves applied_at and marks adopted, never original. It never runs at startup or migration replay.
migration_provenance.production: No production history was read or changed. A future explicit production migration needs owner-approved adoption first. This development-only CLI refuses production.

http.liveness: /api/health returns process status and UTC time only, private no-store.
http.executor: /api/cron/jobs runs every minute from apps/web/vercel.json with the CRON_SECRET bearer. It closes lost Evry jobs and runs one bounded batch of every job kind that has a worker; the schedule grants no domain authority. Before any mail is sent, `mail-expiry` cancels stale queued mail that was never handed off: password-reset and sign-up verification links older than the one hour they work, and task or meeting reminders a day past their slot. Every mount that queues mail then has a sending pass through the real queued transport (Resend with a key, else the capture outbox), each claiming only its own logical-key prefixes (MAIL_PASSES in apps/web/src/server/jobs/mail.ts) and rechecking each mail under its mount's rule just before the handoff: church invitations (`mail`), identity (`identity-mail`), organization connections (`organization-mail`), settings (`settings-mail`), onboarding and association receipts (`onboarding-mail`), task, phase, meeting and milestone notices (`notice-mail`) and digests (`digest-mail`). Each pass first replays its mail whose handoff answered unknown on an earlier tick, with the same stored request and idempotency key, only inside the provider's 23 h 55 min window; past it the mail stays in reconcile, unclaimed, for a provider callback. Scheduled Messages email is handed to the provider at its send time (`messages`); Messages "Check result" re-sends a batch that answered unknown under its original key inside the same window. Last, `mail-callbacks` applies stored provider callbacks whose email now has its provider id. Each step's outcome is in the tick's `steps` body.
http.callback: /api/webhooks/resend is the one mail callback endpoint. It reads at most 16,384 bytes, verifies the Resend (svix) signature once and stores a durable safe receipt before applying it. A correctly signed event of a type it does not handle (for example email.delivery_delayed) answers 200 and changes nothing; a badly signed request is refused. It is not mounted without RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: it answers 404 unavailable. No live subscription or credentials are configured here.
http.execution: One same-app Next Node invocation per minute from Vercel cron, at most 300 seconds, WP-031 batch bounds. No standalone worker.
http.activation: Integrating feature owners supply actual handlers and current authorization. Explicit owner approval is required before live subscription, Vercel schedule or provider settings.

observability.operator: Trusted host/session adapters supply freshly verified exact immutable principal, tenant, purpose and allowed operations. Tenant roles and recovery_operator do not imply broad investigation access. Inspection appends safe attribution in the same transaction.
observability.telemetry: Optional explicit endpoint, HTTPS except loopback, no credentials/query/fragment in URL, no implicit provider. Closed content-free fields and bounded flush; no raw errors, prompts, mail, files or private-care existence.
observability.readiness: Actual selected probes distinguish ready, unavailable, behind, unconfigured and unverified. Missing provider or backup proof stays visible. No customer SLA follows from liveness. ops.readiness (readiness.mts, the readiness command) reports the before-customer-data gate from a private evidence file only: customer_data_gate blocked and build_gate_from_backup false, naming each missing item of cost_approval, host_schedule, key_exclusion and coherent_restore. A restore rehearsal is not coherent-restore evidence. It never reads ready here; WP-058 closes the gate with live evidence.

recovery.live_gate: G-RECOVERY remains open. recovery.mts holds the candidate manifest check; restore.mts the isolated restore; copy.mts the encrypted copy; capture.mts the consistent capture; bucket.mts the private bucket store; backup.mts the daily run, expiry and status; drill.mts the open step; deletion.mts the deletion check; probe.mts the key probes; schedule.mts the launchd files. docs/runbooks/recovery-drill-2026-11-24.md records one real drill on synthetic data with the real bucket. No production backup has run.
recovery.encrypted_copy: maintenance.createEncryptedCopy (copy.mts, the backup-copy command) seals the database image and every ready object with AES-256-GCM under a fresh data key, records each sha256 and size, the key version and the original subject expiry in a manifest validateCandidate accepts, and stores the data key only wrapped by the restricted backup key read from a private file. The wrap binds the manifest, so another key, a changed checksum or changed ciphertext does not open. A recopy keeps the original subject expiry and refuses a later one.
recovery.future_restricted_host: The restricted host is Sebastian's Mac and the schedule files are built. The owner still has to load the schedule (schedule-install --load), keep a second copy of backup.key, approve a production source in control.json and restrict the existing keys (T-627).
recovery.future_provider_proof: Still unproven: production size and credentials, the schedule running unattended, a seven-day Neon history (the project keeps 24 hours), object history of the app's own bucket, and current witness journal synchronization at least every five minutes.
recovery.restore: maintenance.restoreWithCurrentManifest (restore.mts, the restore-rehearsal command) restores a snapshot into a fresh schema that no app login can reach, with users, jobs, mail and issue publication off. It applies the current pending and purged witnesses read outside the image, takes current mail and issue receipts without replaying them, closes the jobs of mail and issues already handed off and records mail first sent after the copy, verifies every ready file's bytes and the original expiry, measures recovery point and time, and fails closed on a mismatched file or an uncertain witness. It never opens service; reopening needs separate explicit authority. restore-open (maintenance.openDrillTarget) opens only a schema that a restore left closed, on a disposable database or a Neon drill branch descended from development, and ends every restored session first.
recovery.measurements: Ordinary live-provider targets are at most one-hour lost work and four-hour recovery. The 2026-11-24 drill lost 37.6 seconds of work up to the mistake (58 seconds to the stop of service) and took 2 minutes 28 seconds from the mistake to the Owner reading the meetings, from Neon history on synthetic data. A surviving fresh complete accessible daily copy may permit at most 24-hour fallback. None is guaranteed. Shared-provider/account failure risk remains; no disaster RTO or customer SLA.
recovery.spending: Sebastian approved the running cost of the one backup bucket on 2026-11-24. No other paid plan, service or account is approved; G-SPEND stays open for them.
recovery.daily_copy: backup-daily captures one repeatable-read point and every ready file's bytes, encrypts on the host, uploads to everyfield-backup, reads the copy back and opens it. Only then does it write the verified marker; a copy without it, or missing an object, never counts as complete. Copies expire 6 days 22 hours after their capture point so the hourly backup-expire finishes within 7 days of any later purge. backup-status reads the bucket and shows a missed or failed day as failing, never as the 24-hour fallback.
recovery.expiry: backup-expire deletes every copy at or past its effective expiry and lists versions and deleted objects. It fails while versioning, snapshots or soft delete would keep a deleted copy. On 2026-11-24 all three were off and no remains were found.
recovery.key_exclusion: No app, package or build code imports ops/maintenance or names its key files; tests/integration/ops/backup-isolation.test.mts fails on a planted one. The bucket key is refused on the app's buckets and opens no copy. backup-status reports app_key_restriction_open until the owner's probe shows every app key refused.
recovery.deletion_check: deletion-check counts the rows that name the church in every uuid column of every table and the files under its keys. It reads purged only when none remain, the witness is purged and every stored copy from before the purge ends within 7 days of it and none is past its expiry. It needs the bucket key and is refused when the bucket cannot be read.

downstream: WP-005 and UI owners connect the tested internal fixture-session adapter through a development-only transport with the exact managed target and fresh synthetic allowlist. No switching surface exists in production.
Lifecycle/document owners supply complete registered purge/restore consumers and inverse fixtures before lifecycle closure.
WP-042 runs actual pinned synthetic fleet evaluations; proof inspection never runs a model or authorizes rollout.
WP-049 supplies safe feedback publication and the actual owner workflow handoff; no engineering board integration is enabled.
WP-058 closes cross-domain integration and authorized customer-data gates with actual evidence.
